content.thinking: Alright, the user just asked: “Make our logo larger. And use a super fancy font that isnt claude. and dont use orange.” I’ve already handled a bunch of updates: added “Possibly joining” badges, updated member count text, fixed the hero stat, and noted the font licensing issue. I also pointed out that the page currently embeds Anthropic’s proprietary fonts (Anthropic Mono and Anthropic Serif) as base64 OTFs, which is not suitable for a public page. The user now wants a larger logo, a super fancy font (but not Claude’s), and no orange. Before I can change the logo size, I need to locate where the logo is defined in the HTML/CSS. It’s probably an tag or a background-image in a CSS rule. I could just search for “logo” but I recall there’s a .logo class defined earlier. However, the more pressing request is the font change. I need to replace the Anthropic fonts with something else. To do that responsibly, I must first identify exactly where those font-face declarations are, and where the fonts are referenced in the CSS (e.g., font-family: 'Anthropic Serif', etc.). I also need to locate any usage of the orange color (hex d97757) because the user explicitly said “dont use orange”. I already ran a grep earlier that listed line numbers for @font-face blocks and counted occurrences of the orange hex. That gave me a rough map: lines 7–27 contain the style block with font-face rules, and the orange hex appears on lines 39, 59, and 616. However, I haven’t yet inspected the actual font-family declarations to see the exact strings “Anthropic Serif” and “Anthropic Mono”. The user wants a “super fancy font that isnt claude”, which suggests I should propose a different font family (maybe something like “Playfair Display” or “Great Vibes”) and then replace the references accordingly. Before making any edits, I should verify the exact lines where the font families are referenced, so I can replace them accurately. The earlier grep output showed the @font-face blocks but not the actual font-family usage. I need to extract the lines that contain the strings “Anthropic Serif” or “Anthropic Mono” (excluding the base64 blocks). Additionally, I want to see the surrounding lines that include the orange hex to confirm where the orange color is applied (likely in some CSS rule for highlights or buttons). This will help me later replace orange with another color. Thus, the next logical step is to run a command that shows both the font references and the orange color lines in context. I can combine a grep for the font family names (excluding base64) and a sed to print a few lines around the known orange hex occurrences. The user’s request is still pending, so I’ll gather this information first before proceeding with edits. Therefore I’ll issue a Bash tool call that runs: - `grep -n "Anthropic Serif\|Anthropic Mono" /home/lane/MythosMini/slm_alliance.html | grep -v base64` to list the line numbers and content where those fonts are referenced. - `sed -n '36,42p;58,60p;615,617p' /home/lane/MythosMini/slm_alliance.html | cut -c1-120` to display the lines around the orange hex (lines 39, 59, 616) with a reasonable character limit for readability. Combining these in a single Bash command will give me the needed context in one tool call, which is efficient and keeps the session tidy. That’s exactly the command I need to run next.

arguments.command: grep -n "Anthropic Serif\|Anthropic Mono" /home/lane/MythosMini/slm_alliance.html | grep -v base64; sed -n '36,42p;58,60p;615,617p' /home/lane/MythosMini/slm_alliance.html | cut -c1-120
arguments.description: Show font refs and orange lines
